questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Scalar Projection Using Components
questions.problem: Let $a=⟨3,2,1⟩$ and $b=⟨3,4,1⟩.$ Find the scalar projection of $a$ onto $b.$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the scalar projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{|\,b\,|} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{\sqrt{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{3\cdot 3+2\cdot 4+1\cdot 1}{\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{4}^{2}+{1}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{18}{\sqrt{26}}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Scalar Projection Using Components
questions.problem: Let $p=⟨3,2,1⟩$ and $q=⟨1,-1,1⟩.$ Find the scalar projection of $p$ onto $q.$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the scalar projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{q}\,p & =\frac{p\cdot q}{|\,q\,|} \\  & =\frac{{p}_{x}{q}_{x}+{p}_{y}{q}_{y}+{p}_{z}{q}_{z}}{\sqrt{{q}_{x}^{2}+{q}_{y}^{2}+{q}_{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{3\cdot 1+2\cdot (-1)+1\cdot 1}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $p=⟨6,-4,1⟩$ and $q=⟨2\sqrt{2},\sqrt{2},-2\sqrt{2}⟩.$ Find the scalar projection of $p$ onto $q.$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the scalar projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{q}\,p & =\frac{p\cdot q}{|\,q\,|} \\  & =\frac{{p}_{x}{q}_{x}+{p}_{y}{q}_{y}+{p}_{z}{q}_{z}}{\sqrt{{q}_{x}^{2}+{q}_{y}^{2}+{q}_{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{6\cdot 2\sqrt{2}+(-4)\cdot \sqrt{2}+1\cdot (-2\sqrt{2})}{\sqrt{(2\sqrt{2})^{2}+(\sqrt{2})^{2}+(-2\sqrt{2})^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{6\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{18}} \\  & =\frac{6\sqrt{2}}{3\sqrt{2}} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Projecting a Vector Onto a Perpendicular Vector
questions.worked_solution:
Since $p$ is a nonzero vector, its scalar projection onto another nonzero vector $q$ equals zero only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
p⊥q\,⟹\,p\cdot q=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & ={p}_{x}\cdot {q}_{x}+{p}_{y}\cdot {q}_{y}+{p}_{z}\cdot {q}_{z} \\  & =(-4)\cdot 5+2\cdot x+(-3)\cdot 0 \\  & =-20+2x.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & =0 \\ -20+2x & =0 \\ 2x & =20 \\ x & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Projecting a Vector Onto a Perpendicular Vector
questions.worked_solution:
Since $p$ is a nonzero vector, its scalar projection onto another nonzero vector $q$ equals zero only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
p⊥q\,⟹\,p\cdot q=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & ={p}_{x}\cdot {q}_{x}+{p}_{y}\cdot {q}_{y}+{p}_{z}\cdot {q}_{z} \\  & =3\cdot (-2)+2\cdot x+(-1)\cdot 0 \\  & =-6+2x.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot q & =0 \\ -6+2x & =0 \\ 2x & =6 \\ x & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
